entries.title: Manthali (Ramechhap) to Lukla Flights: The Complete Guide
entries.excerpt: When Lukla flights leave from Ramechhap, which airlines fly the route, flight time, baggage limits, weather delays and why to sleep in Manthali the night before.
entries.content:
Why Lukla flights leave from Manthali

Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport gets extremely busy in the trekking seasons. To ease the congestion, Nepal's Civil Aviation Authority moves scheduled Lukla flights to Ramechhap Airport in Manthali during the peak spring and autumn seasons. From 25 September 2025, for example, all scheduled Lukla flights were operated from Ramechhap instead of Kathmandu.

The exact dates change from year to year, and outside the peak seasons most Lukla flights go from Kathmandu again. Always check with your airline or trekking agency which airport your flight leaves from.

Airlines flying Manthali to Lukla

Three airlines fly small STOL (short take-off and landing) aircraft on the route. Tickets are sold by the airlines and by trekking agencies. We do not sell flight tickets, but here is how to reach each airline:

Photo: Himalayanasiatreks, CC BY-SA 4.0

[airlines]

Flight time and what to expect

The flight takes about 15–25 minutes, shorter than the flight from Kathmandu. Flights leave early in the morning, usually between about 6 and 10 AM, when mountain weather tends to be calmest. Arrive at the terminal early: your airline or agency will tell you your check-in time.

You land at Lukla's Tenzing-Hillary Airport, a short, sloping airstrip at about 2,850 m. Only small aircraft can use it, which is why seats and baggage space are limited.

Photo: Petr Meissner, CC BY 2.0

Baggage limits

Because the planes are small, baggage limits are strict. A common allowance is 10 kg of checked baggage plus 5 kg of hand luggage per passenger, but it varies by airline and ticket. Extra weight is charged and only carried if there is space, so check your allowance when you book.

Photo: Treflyn, CC BY-SA 4.0

Leave the rest with us

Staying with us before your trek? We can store your extra bags until you are back from the mountains.

Weather, delays and cancellations

Lukla flights depend on the weather. Pilots need good visibility at Lukla and along the route, so cloud or wind in the mountains can delay or cancel flights even on a clear morning in Manthali. Here are the conditions right now:

[weather]

If your flight is held or cancelled, read our guide to Lukla flight delays and cancellations.

Getting to Manthali in time

Ramechhap Airport is about 130–145 km from Kathmandu, a 4–5 hour drive along the BP Highway. To catch a morning flight, many trekkers leave Kathmandu between 1 and 3 AM. The easier option is to drive the day before and sleep in Manthali. See how to get from Kathmandu to Manthali.

[booking Sleep 500 m from the terminal | Arrive the evening before, have dinner on our rooftop and walk to the airport in the morning, rested.]

Your night before the flight

  • About 500 m from the terminal: an easy walk or a very short ride

  • Air-conditioned rooms with a private bathroom and hot shower

  • Rooftop restaurant, with breakfast and room service available

  • Free Wi-Fi to follow flight updates

  • Luggage storage while you trek

entries.title: Kathmandu to Manthali (Ramechhap Airport): How to Get There
entries.excerpt: Distance, route, drive time and transport options from Kathmandu to Manthali and Ramechhap Airport, plus whether to drive through the night or arrive the day before your Lukla flight.
entries.content:
The route

Most drivers leave the Kathmandu Valley through Bhaktapur and Dhulikhel, then follow the BP Highway down towards the Sunkoshi River and turn off at Khurkot onto the road to Manthali, the headquarters of Ramechhap district.

Photo: Bijay Chaurasia, CC BY-SA 4.0

[map Driving route from Kathmandu to Manthali | https://maps.google.com/maps?saddr=Thamel,+Kathmandu&daddr=Ramechhap+Airport,+Manthali&output=embed]

How long it takes

Plan on 4–5 hours for the drive. Traffic leaving Kathmandu, roadworks and landslides in the monsoon can make it longer. In October 2025, for example, floods and landslides damaged parts of the BP Highway and traffic had to be diverted, so check the road before you set off.

Ways to travel

  • Private car or jeep: most trekking agencies arrange one as part of your package, and you can also hire one in Kathmandu.

  • Shared jeeps and tourist buses: in the trekking seasons they run between Kathmandu and Manthali, often overnight to reach the morning flights. Ask your agency or your Kathmandu hotel about current departures.

  • Local buses: the cheapest and slowest option. Ask locally for the latest times.

Drive through the night, or arrive the day before?

[compare]

Night drive

  • Leave Kathmandu around 1–3 AM

  • No extra hotel night

  • Little sleep before the flight

  • A slow road can make you late for check-in

Arrive the day before (recommended)

  • Drive in daylight and see the valley

  • Sleep 500 m from the terminal

  • A calm, rested start to your trek

  • A buffer if the weather holds flights

[/compare]

[booking Break the journey in Manthali | Drive down in daylight, stay with us and walk to the airport in the morning.]

Arriving in Manthali

We are on the Lamosangu–Ramechhap Highway at Manthali Bus Stand, about 300 m from the bus park and 500 m from the airport. See our location page for the map and directions.

entries.title: Lukla Flight Delayed or Cancelled? What to Do in Manthali
entries.excerpt: Why Lukla flights get delayed or cancelled, what to do at Ramechhap Airport, your options if the weather will not clear, how to spend a delay day in Manthali, and where to stay near the airport tonight.
entries.content:
Why Lukla flights get cancelled

Flights to Lukla fly by sight into a short mountain airstrip, so pilots need clear visibility at Lukla and along the route. Cloud or wind in the mountains can hold flights even when the sky over Manthali is blue. When a morning is lost, the backlog of passengers can take a day or more to clear.

Photo: James Heilman, CC BY-SA 3.0

[weather]

What to do if your flight is held

  1. Stay in touch with your airline or agency. They announce new departure times and rebook passengers.

  2. Keep your ticket, ID and hand luggage with you while you wait.

  3. If flights are called off for the day, ask about your place on the next flights and find a bed close to the airport.

  4. Keep a spare day or two in your itinerary, for the flight back from Lukla too.

If the weather will not clear

  • Wait for the next flight: usually the cheapest option.

  • Helicopter: charter or shared seats cost more. Ask your agency, and check whether your travel insurance covers it.

  • Another route: some agencies can arrange road transport into the Solukhumbu region instead. Ask yours.

Making the most of a delay day

Rebooked onto a later flight, or told there are no more flights today? Then the day is yours. If you are still on standby, keep your phone charged and switched on and stay within easy reach of the terminal: the airline may call you back at short notice when the weather clears. Here is an easy plan for a free day, all on foot from the hotel:

Time

What to do

06:00–08:00

Walk into Manthali bazaar for a hot milk tea, and take out cash while you are there. The banks are about 1 km from the hotel: see them on our area map.

08:30–09:30

Watch the airstrip from our rooftop, or ask us the way to Selfie Danda, a small hill near the runway with a view over the airport and the valley.

10:00–13:00

Walk down past the runway to the wide bed of the Tamakoshi River, about 15 minutes away, and watch valley life along the water.

13:30–15:00

Lunch in the bazaar, or dal bhat on our rooftop.

16:00–18:30

Walk up the ridge behind the airport for sunset over the valley, and head back before the evening chill.

Grounded for the whole day? Khandadevi Temple, a hilltop temple and viewpoint, is about 1 hr 15 min away by hired jeep. Only go once your airline has confirmed there are no more flights today.

Bring cash from Kathmandu

ATMs in Manthali can run out of cash in the busy trekking seasons, so carry enough rupees for your stay and for your trek.

Useful Nepali phrases for the bazaar

Shopkeepers are used to trekkers, and a few words of Nepali go a long way:

English

Nepali

When to use it

Hello

Namaste

A greeting for anyone, at any time of day

How much is this?

Yasko kati ho?

Asking the price in a shop

Where is the ATM?

ATM kaha cha?

Finding a cash point

Where is the pharmacy?

Medical kaha cha?

Pharmacies are usually called “medical” in Nepal

Is there water?

Paani cha?

Buying bottled drinking water

Thank you

Dhanyabaad

Showing appreciation

That’s very expensive!

Ekdam mahango bhayo!

Friendly bargaining, with a smile

[booking Need a room tonight? | Stay 500 m from the terminal: air-conditioned rooms, hot showers, free Wi-Fi to follow flight updates, a rooftop restaurant and luggage storage. Call or WhatsApp us to check what is free tonight.]

Plan ahead for next time

Arriving in Manthali the day before your flight gives you a calmer start and a buffer if the weather is slow to clear. See how to get from Kathmandu to Manthali and our Manthali to Lukla flight guide.

sections.heading: Start your Everest journey *rested*
sections.text: In peak trekking season, many Lukla flights leave from Manthali (Ramechhap) Airport. Drive in from Kathmandu the day before and stay with us. Then it's a short trip to the airport in the morning.

sections.note: Flights usually leave early in the morning and move with the weather. Tickets are booked with the airline or your trekking agency, so always confirm your departure time with them. [Read our Manthali to Lukla flight guide →](/guides/manthali-to-lukla-flights)

tips.title: Confirm the evening before
tips.text: Lukla schedules move with the mountain weather. Check your flight time with your airline or agency the evening before, and again in the morning.

tips.title: Pack light, leave the rest
tips.text: Lukla flights have strict baggage limits, so check yours with the airline. Leave extra bags with us while you trek.

tips.title: 500 m to the terminal
tips.text: Wake up close to Manthali Airport: an easy walk or a very short ride, with no pre-dawn drive from Kathmandu.

sections.heading: Cooked fresh, *Nepali* style
sections.lead: "Dal bhat power, 24 hour!" There's no better fuel before the mountains.
sections.text: We cook everything fresh for our guests. You can have a full Nepali thali with rice, dal, seasonal greens and pickles, or a quick breakfast before the airport. Groups are welcome and we're happy to cater for vegetarians. Prefer to eat in? Room service is available.

sections.heading: Where travellers *meet*
sections.text: Pull up a chair, order a pot of tea and watch the hills. Trekking groups love our rooftop for dinner the night before they fly.

sections.heading: Manthali *in 3D*
sections.text: The walk to the airport, the drive from Kathmandu and the flight to Lukla, over the real terrain. Tap a place for details.

items.title: From Kathmandu
items.text: By road via the BP Highway and Lamosangu–Ramechhap Highway. Tourist jeeps and buses run daily.

items.title: From the airport
items.text: Manthali (Ramechhap) Airport is about 500 m away, an easy walk or a very short ride. Ask us about getting to your early flight.

items.title: From the bus park
items.text: Manthali Bus Park is about 300 m away, a short walk with your bags.

sections.heading: Flying to Lukla from *Ramechhap*
sections.text: During the busy trekking seasons, many Lukla flights for the Everest region leave from Manthali (Ramechhap) Airport rather than Kathmandu. Flights usually go early in the morning, when the weather is clearest.
